reason: The hypothesis relies on the claim that the FeCrNiTiZr HEA is an excellent repair material with good wear resistance (E1), but E1 only studies coating on H13 steel, not repair of a damaged, hot-cracking-prone component. E2 provides general background on laser cladding but is incomplete and does not address hot-cracking mitigation or repair of a damaged part. The key premise that laser cladding avoids hot cracking in a repair context is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Laser cladding can deposit a crack-free, metallurgically bonded HEA layer on a hot-cracking-prone substrate.
The FeCrNiTiZr HEA coating exhibits high hardness and good elevated-temperature wear resistance.
Rapid solidification in laser cladding avoids low-melting phases and wide freezing ranges that cause hot cracking.
The HEA coating can serve as an excellent repair material for H13 hot-working tool steel.
